title: The Ravens Have a Receiver Problem

text: Uh, so I want to start off with, um, I want to give prayers and condolences, uh, to the Herbert family. Uh, there's been some, you know, some, uh, high-level, inflection points, uh, but it's been, uh, it's been it's been just a real steady climb to, um, our ultimate goal for the offseason, which was to get the best and most healthy team, uh, to training camp. And, I think they have a good understanding of of what needs to happen, which is balance, you know, get a take a break from football, uh but also mesh business and pleasure. Uh and that's that's um you know, getting themselves getting themselves ready for training camp where you have to you have to be in the best shape of your life. title: Super Bowl champ Willie Colon on Knicks parade, Jaxson Dart's growth, Jets' blueprint, lupus support
text: All right, welcome to Talking Ball with Pat Leonard, a return special guest to the program, Super Bowl champion, sports analyst, die-hard Knicks fan, Willie Colon in the house. What is up, Willie? Thanks for returning to the program here. >> Man, can't thank you enough. I appreciate you and all your efforts, man, and I'm glad to be back on. >> Yeah, so you're here courtesy of your annual golf outing. It's the Willie Colon golf outing, Monday, June 22nd, 12th annual at Canoe Brook Country Club in Summit, New Jersey, benefiting the Lupus Research Alliance. Willie, can you just remind everybody why this is such an important cause and why it's so uh meaningful to you as well, and why you host this event every year? >> Yeah, so my my mother was diagnosed with lupus. She's no no longer with us. Excuse me. Um she's you know, when I was able to get drafted to the Pittsburgh Steelers, you know, I I wanted to use my platform and raise awareness about the disease and um just bring to light all you know, all the I think the Lupus community is trying to do, which is is find a cure, um find money to build, you know, find money to kind of help, you know, find the necessary research and and and and and really just do a better job of, you know, bringing awareness and and helping people cope with the disease and learn about it. So, it's it's a lot and we just try to do I just try to do my part with the with the Lupus Foundation and um it just really just be a flag bearer, right? And I think that's the goal, just trying to raise awareness, find a cure, and then continue to build. >> He Willie does great work with this every year. A very inclusive event, a very well-attended event. Honestly, most of these events you you see the list of people who are supposed to show up, and then it's probably two out of every 10 that actually show up. All of Willie's people roll up. I'm telling you, they all roll up, they all roll in, they're always there for you, and it reflects well on you, sir. Uh to donate, everybody, to support the cause, go to give.lupusresearch.org. And again, that's the Willie Colon Golf Outing, 12th annual at Canoe Brook Country Club in Summit, New Jersey, Monday, June 22nd coming up. All right, so Willie, you're in celebration mode right now. I've been following you on social media, man. New York Knicks ending a 53-year championship drought. Can you just tell me, what are your what are your emotions and thoughts right now coursing through you? Cuz I can tell from the limited amount I've seen on social that um for you, it's just been like a release of a lot of emotion here. >> Yeah, man, it's you know, I think and I'm not the only one that shares these emotions. I think if you've been kind of combing through social media, you've seen a lot of middle-aged men have emotional breakdowns over the the win the big win, you know, and I think it starts from uh for me, for sure, it starts back in my my childhood, you know, I remember growing up in the South Bronx living in my two-bedroom apartment, uh my whole family, and you know, my dad was a big sports guy. He loved the Knicks, he loved the Giants, and uh Yankees, but the Knicks was like his thing. Like, he loved the Knicks, and and so I would, you know, our time together was sitting at the edge of his bed watching the Knicks, right? And then he would just, you know, tell me he would talk about his life, my family, you know, this father-son stuff, and he would he would just pour in life into me, and so while doing all that, we were still focused on the Knicks, and you know, when you grow up watching those '90s Knicks with Ewing and then Oakley and Mason and and Starks and Harper and the list goes on. We had some really good teams, some really strong teams, but we always lost, right? And so I, you know, that was the time when Jordan was king and so Jordan sent me to bed crying a lot. Uh him and Reggie Miller and even when you know, Jordan decided to go play baseball, we had a shot against the Houston Rockets and we lost that series, right? And so it's been years and years of just disappointment. Even in '99 when we had a shot to beat the Spurs, you know, we lost that one. So, and then I you know, from that from then on I've seen a lot of bad Knicks teams, right? And and it's unfortunate to those guys cuz it was just a you know, it just the teams weren't very good, but it was just years and years not having the team I grew up loving be relevant in any regard in any regard. So, now that the Knicks are not only champions, man, they've healed a lot of my childhood trauma. Uh so, I'm I'm I'm fortunate, man. I'm blessed and I'm extremely happy. >> No, that's awesome. Congratulations. I want to follow up with you know, you are a Super Bowl champion, won Super Bowl 43 with the Pittsburgh Steelers in February 2009, a famously dramatic ending, 27-23, Steelers over the Cardinals. How do you compare the emotions of being a player achieving your career goal and then on the other side of it, like the die-hard fan watching your team win? Like what How How similar or different are those emotions? >> It's very different. It is very different, you know. Me me winning my Super Bowl was surreal in so many ways. Like I at first being on a championship team, a championship team, a historic team, the way we had, you know, the the journey we took to get to the Super Bowl was was was daunting in itself. I tell everybody I try to remind people we played the Baltimore Ravens when they were at the height of being the Baltimore Ravens, where they were like the you know, and we had to do that we had to beat them three times to get to the Super Bowl. So, I try to tell everybody when I got to the Super Bowl, I was tanked, man. I had to have mentally, physically, spiritually, I you know, I came from Hofstra where we only played 10 games, you know what I mean? And so, we we didn't There was no We didn't go to the playoffs. So, to go on that journey and every game and you know how it is, Pat, cuz you you're in the trenches. You know, when you get into the playoffs, not just the playoffs, but like the back in the before you get into the playoffs, that month of December, man, it's a dog fight cuz everybody's scrapping to get to the table. You You guys are injured. You don't know who you have. You're playing through injuries and it's it's just a fight and fight and then, you know, we were fortunate enough to uh be the one seed. But, it when you're the one seed, so much Everybody's gunning for you, right? And so, you're you're you're in some real dog battles. With all that said, man, um the journey, winning it the way we won it, um I was just I was on zero. So, the parade, I remember, you know, coming down the day. Actually, Pittsburgh has an Avenues of America, too. I don't think people know that. So, turning down the Avenue of of Americas, seeing the confetti, was just like it was the perfect ending. And I I think I partied all the way up to the next the next season. I had to remind myself that this is a whole new season. Uh and I think the rest of the team had to do the same. >> So, that was more like an exhale of finally getting there, whereas the >> Yeah, and and not to cut you off the like the Knicks the Knicks the Knicks parade is more full circle cuz I was a kid who watched the games with my dad and now I'm a dad being able to watch a Knicks parade with my son. So, that's why it's it's it's two different. So, it's just it's it's an emotional ride, but uh you know, it's just I I never thought I would see one. Just never thought I would see one. So. >> Very cool. All right, shifting to football, some quick football talk because you know all about the NFL and including New York football and you know, the Giants have a new head coach in John Harbaugh, and he's been the focus, but Willie, you know that no matter what else changes on a roster, different players around this this player, or even the head coach or GM, if your quarterback's good, you have a chance. We all know the kid's athletic. I think I think we you know horse to death as far as his ability to to learn, like he has to, you know, run out of bounds, and then they realize he can't take the hit state he used to take in college, and you know, that's kind of hopefully all that's behind him. But I think the kid is going to be a stud, and I think John Harbaugh I think what he's done to First of all, I think personally, with him, I thought he's done a phenomenal job of handling the media market here in New York. I thought he's done a great job of putting out small fires. I think he really has an idea and a vision and a blueprint on what he wants the team to look like, and I think it starts defensively. I think he wants his defense to be a defense that causes a lot of chaos, and I think he wants a defense that really a lot of what they did in Baltimore, cuz I played against them. That That was a black and blue defense. Like they they put a hurting on you, right? They want They want to play a physical brand of football, and he wants to bring that back to the Giants, and the Giants were that at one point before things kind of fell apart for them defensively. But when you have a good defense, that just backs up a young quarterback, right? That allows a young quarterback to grow. That allows a young quarterback to not feel like he has to shoulder all the wins, right? Like he he can he can say, "Hey man, if things don't go right for me, I know I have defense that get get me back to football. title: PFT PM Mailbag: Mike Vrabel's future, collective bargaining in CFB | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: It's time to answer a few questions before we wrap this up. Kristen, go ahead and fire up the first one. We have pre-selected a handful of questions that were submitted today. Berg asks or says before he asks, "The NFL no longer has an official sports book sponsorship since the FanDuel one expired. They also had sponsorships with DraftKings and I think BetMGM. Seeing how the Sources B situation is going to play out, how will they mitigate a new deal while also getting or dealing, excuse me, with a potential Sources B punishment?" Hey, this is the great hypocrisy that the NFL will be dealing with. Do as we say, not as we do. They already do it when it comes to equity ownership. Any owner can own up to 5% of any company that operates a sports book. Players can't do advertising, can't own a piece, can't do anything, can't touch that flame at all. The owners, they can they can turn that flame all the way up to 5% of a multi-billion dollar company. As many of them as they want. 5% of FanDuel, 5% of DraftKings, 5% of this one, 5% of that one. They can do it and they won't tell us who owns what. They'll tell us they're allowed to do it, but they won't say who owns what. Yeah, it's hypocritical. Especially because Sources B is a product of an era where he grew up with gambling not just legalized, but normalized. Ads everywhere. Apps on your phone. There's nothing wrong with it anymore. Everyone does it. If you don't do it, you're not cool. I mean, it's like the beer commercials and the soda commercials. They're trying to get you to think your life isn't complete unless you're engaging in this activity. And you're 18. And you like to compete, you like that rush. I can see how a guy like Brendon Sources B very easily ends up down that path. And the NFL's got to reconcile that. Well, they don't have to. They don't have to do anything that they don't want to do. But I think from an outsider's perspective, it's fair to say, "How could you even think about suspending Brandon Staley for being one of the many victims?" And I know victims may be a strong word, but maybe not. Of this age where everywhere you look, it's bet, bet, bet, bet, bet, and it taps right into the psyche of an 18-year-old boy who loves the idea of winning $2 here and $2 there cuz it gives him that little dopamine rush. So, the NFL will have sports book sponsors by the time the season starts. There's nothing to sponsor now. You don't need a sports book sponsor when there aren't games. I would suggest by the time the season begins, they will have one or two or three. I think at one point they had seven sports book sponsors. They're going to take the money from whoever will give it to them. And I suspect multiple companies will be giving them a lot of money by the time the season begins. All right, next question. From Nick Watt. Is NFL a real sport or just an entertainment that can be manipulated at will and doesn't amount to anything? Has Goodell gone too far with the sports entertainment stuff? I don't know what sports entertainment stuff you're referring to, Nick, but I'm a firm believer that the NFL does not rig games. Now, it's kind of cute how they lean into the whole the NFL is scripted thing. Nothing's scripted. Nothing's predetermined. They're not devising in advance who's going to win this game or that game. I remember when the Chiefs were getting the beneficiaries of a lot of calls, and there was some conspiracy theory about the Chiefs getting favorable treatment because the NFL wanted them to keep winning. And I will acknowledge at some level if your game officials hear enough from the structure above them how valuable it is to have the Chiefs continue to advance through high-profile games. Does it influence you at some point when you're calling the flags or not calling them in real time? Maybe it does. Maybe it does, but there's no script. There's no rigging. There could be some subconscious bias that creeps into the minds of the officials who know that it's better for the league to have the Chiefs in the Super Bowl than the Jaguars. Sorry, Jaguars, but you know it's true. But but it's legitimate competition. And it's not like basketball where the officials can have, I think, a huge impact on extending a series from four games to five, which I I kind of think happened in game three. I kind of think that happened. You look at the disparity in foul calls. Yeah, I think that they they didn't want a sweep. And you could argue they were trying to extend it to game six with some of the non-calls and calls that were made on Saturday night. The Knicks overcame that. So, it's not rigged. It's all legitimate, but I will acknowledge there could be some subconscious biases that creep into the minds of the officials based upon the perception or the reality that certain teams are more valuable to the NFL if they get to the Super Bowl or deeper into the postseason than others. All right, next Chuck While a CBA would be a simple way to fix college football at this point, why would the players agree to it when they basically can do and get paid what they want now? That is an excellent point, and you know, this question comes up on the day that the Protect College Sports Act has made its way out of committee in the Senate. It's going to have a full vote. They're working on amendments. There's an avalanche of different little news nuggets about this aspect of the bill and that aspect of the bill, but for the first time, there's going to be a floor vote on a bill aimed at protecting college sports from college sports. I, as you know, I don't like any of this. I think that the people who made the mess should be the ones to clean it up. That the college system through the big revenue sports, they managed to find a way to violate the antitrust laws for decades. There's finally been the reckoning, and now they want someone else to fix it. They're the kid that's holding up the broken toy asking Mommy or Daddy to fix it. Well, they should be expected to fix it themselves. Comply with the laws. Find a way to exist in an environment that has laws that apply to all American companies. That's what capitalism is. You don't get a handout. You don't get it to be socialism whenever you want it to be socialism. You got to go compete. And I've been a firm believer in collective bargaining. Now, I saw that Senator Maria Cantwell, one of the sponsors of the Protect College Sports Act, has explained that it would be difficult because you need a federal act. You you you you could do whatever you want to do. They could set the stage to have collective bargaining. I know that state employees can't collectively bargain, but you can change the laws the same way they tried to change the laws as it relates to the antitrust laws. They could change the laws and empower the state-owned and operated colleges to engage in collective bargaining. And if there's some state that doesn't want to be in on it, then you're not part of the NCAA. If you want to opt out of the broader NCAA system, hey California, if you don't want to do this, then none of your schools are part of this process, and all the players will go elsewhere. Everybody will do it. Whatever it takes. If that's ultimately the solution, they'll all line up. They'll all change whatever laws they have to change to have collective bargaining. But, the other point and this is the one that Chuck raises. From the players' perspective, why do we want to unionize? We got a pretty good deal here. Chaos is good for us. We can go to any team anytime we want. We can get paid as much money as we can make. Why do we want to sign on to a CBA that would limit our power? Well, one reason to do it, and this is why the colleges don't want it, when you have a union at the table banging for your rights, you may not have as many padded practices. You may not be expected to show up for voluntary conditioning all throughout the off season. You have a little control. Maybe a a a more safe environment. Because, for example, something Nick Saban used to do. He'd bring some of his former players who had played in the NFL back to practice against the college kids. Trent Richardson. Years after he'd left Alabama was back in full pads practicing against Alabama players. If you have a union, the union's going to say, "Wait a minute, we don't want a 27-year-old man practicing against an 18-year-old boy." a union would give the player greater protection. A union would push back against some of the things that the schools are doing. But, it is a great point. To get me to sign a union card, to get me to vote in favor of having a union, I need to think that I'm going to be better off with a union than I am without one. And right now, I'm in pretty good shape without a union. Maybe that's the next step. Maybe Now, it gets complicated. Maybe the Protect College Sports Act is the thing that galvanizes the players to unionize or try to. And we know there've been efforts in the past. And it's getting harder and harder to say these guys aren't employees. It's getting harder and harder to push back against the idea of collective bargaining. And if there's ever a requirement for federal or state laws to be changed to allow it, if that's the way the ball is moving, everyone is going to move in that direction. I'm confident of that. All right, do we have any more questions? I can't remember. Here's one more. Our good friend Tom Marshall has the variable Ruscin story petered out or will it bounce back before the season? The next big step, well, there's two. And there was a report today. Really wasn't news, but it was an opportunity to say, "What the hell is taking so long for The Athletic to do its internal investigation of Dianna Ruscin?" She resigned more than 2 months ago. It's all died down. Whenever The Athletic says whatever it says, and they probably will announce their findings publicly, even if they may be inviting a lawsuit from Dianna Ruscin, because whatever they provide to their employees privately, somebody's going to leak it. And they've already committed to transparency with the employees. So, I fully expect that there will be an announcement, an explanation of whatever they found. And this isn't whether or not she had an affair with Mike Vrabel. The question is, how did the relationship, to the extent that it was an actual or perceived conflict of interest, affect her reporting? And I think it requires them to go back and look at any of her reports that directly or indirectly relate to Mike Vrabel from the time that she arrived and engage in a very thorough, specific analysis looking at the reporting. Looking at whatever other resources they may have. She doesn't work there, so it makes it harder for them to get answers from her. But, was her reporting in any way affected by the actual or apparent conflict of interest. That's the next development. The development that may happen, may not happen, who knows when it'll happen, Diana Rusini telling her story. She's been very quiet. She's disappeared. There was some tabloid type stuff, TMZ, page six, pictures of her out and about. She hadn't spoken to anyone. I remember when the Patriots got the assignment to start the season Wednesday, September 9, I said, "Boy, Tuesday night, September 8, that's a hell of a time for a live interview with Oprah or Morley Safer or someone where she can tell her whole story. That would throw a hell of a wrench into the week one game between the Patriots and the Seahawks. Because I don't know what she's going to say. And nobody knows what she's going to And she could say something that would create a fresh set of issues for Mike Vrabel. Will she ever tell her story? All we know from her so far is she denies that there was any sort of improper relationship. She said it when the first photos came out. She said it when she resigned. She blamed the media for creating a false narrative. And she said nothing since the more damning group of photos was posted by the New York Post from a Tribeca bar in March of 2020 with Vrabel and Rusini, and she said nothing since Vrabel has addressed the situation multiple times in a way that would undercut his initial denial. That was the moment this thing went off the rails. If they had just not commented in response to the initial photos, it may have died on the vine. Cuz those initial photos, you look at them, it's like, "Yeah, okay." I didn't know what I was going to do with those photos until I scrolled down to the bottom of the story and I saw the denials. Like, "Well, they're on the record. They're denying." That gave this thing a life of its own. And even though it has died down, those are the two big things to watch for. The Athletic and their investigation and if and when Iyanla Simonyi chooses to tell her story. Hi, it's Mike Florio. Thanks for watching PFT on YouTube. Hit subscribe for the latest news and analysis from Pro Football Talk.

I think they would need to do some type of genetic manipulation and cross it with like an emu or an ostrich potentially, and you'd be able to get that same thing. Um so, hey, maybe there's a future for Hall of Fame Farms roid-ed up ostrich emu turkey things. >> I'm in. I'm in. >> Silent partner. >> We're [laughter] in. We'll do it. >> Yeah, I'll take your money all day. >> Um Hall of Fame Farms, by the way, is amazing, and and you guys have gotten the steaks, right? Yes? >> Yes. >> Okay. >> TJ, big order. >> No, I mean, I I tried to get the steaks, I think maybe last time they were out, but I got the uh like the jerky. >> There you go. >> And it was amazing, Joe. It was great. And I have an order coming later. Definitely. >> It's it's amazing stuff. And when you out when you go out to eat with Joe now, like and they they come over and they say, "Hey, and our special of the day is this steak." Whatever. Uh Joe immediately says, "Hey, can you tell me where it's from? Like what farm was it from?" And the waitress has to go back to the kitchen, this happened recently, and come back and report, "Oh, okay." And then Joe maybe orders the steak. But the the reason, one of the reasons I wanted to have you on today, is because you have this new series on your farm in which you invite Hall of Famers to Hall of Fame Farm. And the first episode is hysterical with Jared Allen because of all guys who seemingly know their way around your neck of the woods, so to speak, it's Jared Allen. And he shows up to teach you how to lasso. And you I don't know if you did this on purpose, you threw him off the back of the ATV while he's trying to lasso [clears throat] a steer. Is he okay? Or or a baby calf? Is he okay? >> He did survive, and the reason we were put in the situation is because he's planning to come out, we're going to film the first episode of the Hall of Fame experience, as you mentioned. I've got my farm in Wisconsin, we raise Hall of Fame Wagyu and Angus. Jared Allen grew up on a cutting horse ranch. We're doing a Full Ride Bourbon, which is his new bourbon that he's launching right now, a collaboration with Hall of Fame Farms and Full Ride Bourbon. For Father's Day, we're launching it very soon, so let's do a show. Let's bring him out here, you can be our inaugural episode on YouTube. And he was supposed to bring his horses, which he has a number of them, but he was coming right from his daughter's volleyball tournament somewhere else, and he didn't have time to go to the ranch and hitch up the horses and bring them to Wisconsin. So, he shows up with no horses, but he had a rope. So, when he got in, I said, "Well, we have calves to tag, so we're going to have to figure out how to do this." And we allowed a few calves to get fairly big. Usually, you try to tag them right when they hit the ground, but well, we wanted to save them and see if we could lasso them with Jared's horses. So, no horses, so I said, "Well, do you think we could do it off the back of an ATV?" And he said, "Well, we might as well try it because that's the only way we can find out." So, Jared starts on the back of the ATV, and he's lassoing. And the problem was when he went to throw, he actually got the back leg on the first calf that we drove up on, which was amazing to be able to do that on the back of an ATV. For people that don't know, it's not a smooth ride through the cow-calf pasture on a ATV versus a horse. It's very bumpy, very tricky, and you've got a guy with bad thumbs trying to hit the thumb throttle [clears throat] and make sure we're keeping a perfect speed next to the calf as it's running next to its mom. So, he gets the lasso on the back of the leg, and this is my first time doing it. I got no idea, but he pulls to tighten the lasso, but when he does it, this athletic Hall of Fame Farms Wagyu leaps and jumps through the lasso. So, now the lasso is not on the back of the leg, and so now he thinks it's going to pull tight, right? And he's got to be able to pull the calf legs together and then we jump off and rope it, but it jumps out of the lasso, and so he flips ass over [laughter] teakettle, and I'm going, and I see, and all of a sudden, I feel that everything behind me is getting lighter, and I look around, and there's Jared laying on his back, and I go, "Oh god, we got our first insurance liability claim on the very [laughter] first episode of the Hall of Fame experience. This is not going to be good if I break the leg of my Hall of Fame where I'm supposed to be showing a wonderful Hall of Fame experience on the farm, too." So, it didn't start well, but thank god, the man is a man of steel, and he was no worse for the wear. He got up and we were able to continue the episode with many more roping opportunities. >> It's great stuff. Talking all of Famer Joe Thomas and I did not know this Joe and you seemingly were surprised as well. Jared Allen opens up like he brought all these different kinds of lassos like right out of the box. Yeah, the look on your face. Like so there there are different what like density of cord or length of lasso? Like what what's going on here? >> So I was a shot put discus thrower in high school college and you know you've got your custom shots and discs that have the disc has different weights and different materials, you know, sometimes for different conditions. You got wind, you got no wind, you're you know, trying to do certain things with how it fits just like a golf club to your personal swing and who knew but apparently roping lassos are the same way cuz he showed up with like a branded case, you know, bowling's big in Wisconsin and you know, like the fancy bowlers that are rolling 500s and getting paid, you know, at least tens of dollars as professional bowlers in Wisconsin. [laughter] They've got the fancy bowling cases. So Jared Allen's got his roping case and he's talking about this one's a little bit heavier if you're trying to do this and this one's more stiff and this one's a little bit looser and he's got all these situations and I'm just sitting there like Jared, as long as you got a rope, that's all we need because really I'm not going to be roping any calves. I'm going to try my best but there's no chance of success anyway, so you can just leave the rest of them in the bag. Maybe we'll talk about it uh later at a different point. >> Uh it's great stuff, man. I'm not just saying that like because it's you like I laughed and Jared Allen's the perfect guest. Who who you looking for uh the next guy up or who else is doing the series? >> So we had Jared and then we had Barstool Sports out, Chef Donnie of the great Barstool Sports cooking shows that he's got down there and then Kay Adams who is their college and pro football expert. He's an offensive lineman from Indiana. So those guys came up for two days and the cool thing about Hall of Fame experience and what we're doing with the YouTube is first episode with Jared was a little bit more about just introducing you to the farm, introducing you to some of the the characters, some of the cattlemen, herdsmen that work out here with me. And then each episode with the guest is going to cater to what the guest wants to do, the things that they like to lean into. So Barstool Sports in that experience is going to be totally different. Obviously those guys are hilarious. Chef Donny's an incredible cook. We got him cooking over an open fire up at a campsite that we set up up in the woods. A beautiful setting. We had an incredible night with them. Especially the best part was cameras turned off, everybody left, and it was just the three of us sitting around the fire drinking beer, having laughs, listening to the coyotes howl and the owls hoot in the trees. And it was just really, really fun because of how different and the contrast between we got our roping cattleman, Jared Allen here, and then we got our goofy, more funny, sheffy, more food based show here with Barstool Sports. Then we got Midwest comedian Charlie Berens. We filmed with him last week. So we've got a few in the can that we're putting together, we're editing, and getting ready to release over the next couple weeks. And then we've got unbelievable guests scheduled for the rest of the summer between chefs and musicians and more Hall of Famers and entertainers. And it's been just a lot of fun for me to be able to show people my life, what I've done transferring from the football field now to the farming field and raising cattle and and learning this entire business myself, raising the cattle, and then now selling Hall of Fame Wagyu beef on the other end. It's been amazing and bringing fans and NFL fans and people throughout the country that are interested in farming, interested in all these amazing Hall of Famers, these musicians, these entertainers, and seeing them experience farm life for the first time. It's just been a joy for me even if we didn't do any filming, if we weren't putting anything on our YouTube page. >> And the YouTube page is, and I have it up here, it's Hall of Fame Farms. Hall of Fame Farms, and it's not just the stuff on the farm, like you're hanging out with Jacob Misiorowski as well and some of the Brewers, Ryan Braun, uh which is kind of cool. Can we talk about football here for a second? >> Sure. >> All right. So, for those who don't know, and Joe obviously does, I do the play-by-play for the Browns, and Joe is there with our good friend and amazing broadcaster in his own right, Chris Rose, doing the preseason TV uh for your Cleveland Browns locally. We have three games this year, one of which, by the way, well, of course there are three games in the preseason, but only two for you guys because one of them's going to be an Amazon Prime game, Browns and your Patriots week three of the preseason, a primetime affair. Uh Joe Brox man asked me earlier, "Who starts more games this year, Deshaun or Shaddur?" >> Mhm. >> You want to take a swing at that? >> That's obviously the question everybody in Cleveland is looking to find the answer to. I think coming out of the off season, it seems like Deshaun Watson is probably going to be the guy going into training camp as the starter. He looks pretty healthy coming off that that Achilles tear that he had, and I think the experience that he has playing football, the arm looks like it's still there. The legs look like they've come back, and that's that's one thing Shaddur doesn't exactly bring you right now is the ability to scramble. He's not exceptional at using his legs to get a first down, although he is very good at scrambling to make plays to be able to throw the football. I think Deshaun right now just gives that offense a little bit more versatility to be able to open things up and be more dynamic. Um and I think he'll probably be the guy if I had to bet who's going to start more games this season for the Browns, it would be Deshaun. >> It's funny. I I I went the other way, and I don't know that we know, and I don't know that Todd Monken knows. I don't know that there is a right answer here. I think eventually you got to get to a point where and listen, they they may win games with Deshaun. The defense, I think it's still going to be good. I know it's still going to be good. The question is how good? Like can they actually be carry a team good? And the last 2 years as good as they were, the offense was only scoring 16 points a game. So, no defense is that good. Um eventually you have to turn to the younger guy cuz the younger the the core now is so young. But if Deshaun plays well to your point, let's say he wins the job and he plays well, you're not going to bench him just for the sake of youth. So, it's can he win the job and and how well can he actually play? And and being out there last week for minicamp, look, they both at times looked really good. For both of them, it just comes down to consistency. And you know this, like they're in pajamas. It's not It's a glorified passing camp. It's minicamp. They're in shorts. Like there are no pads. Like can you you can get a feel I think for quarterback play, but you can't get a feel for the line. You can't get a feel for what that defense is truly doing against you until you get to to camp. And I think people were upset because Todd Monken had kind of said that I want to have my guy in place at the end of minicamp. But there's no game on on June 11th. Like I don't Don't you think healthy competition is a good thing for training camp even if it's at quarterback? >> Yeah, definitely competition is always a good thing. I think Todd's words were more to the the line of we want to have a clear starter going in so we know how reps are going to be split up to begin training camp so that all the guys that are going to be working around him, they know who the person is that is going to be under center that they're going to work with. They know the guy that's going to be calling the plays. The receivers have a chance to get ready and prepared for working with Deshaun. Cuz I think it is good knowing at that position at least what the depth chart looks like. And that's not to say it doesn't change in week two, week three, week four as they play preseason games, but I think just having some certainty, so it's not a question that everybody's getting ans- asked every single week. And that's the challenge for those other positions, right? Because when you're a receiver, when you're a tackle, when you're a running back, you want to focus on getting yourself better and being the best version of yourself so you can help your teammates. And if everybody's always asking you, "Who's looking better? Who's number one? Who's taking more reps? What's going on at the quarterback position?" It just puts an extra layer of burden on you as you're trying to figure out your fit within that offense. And so I think Todd just wanted to be able to say, "Hey, we're going to name who's first, who's second, we'll split up the reps, give everybody certainty, and then the competition happens within that structure," which I think gives everybody just a little bit more calm and stability in training camp where their meet of the work for the season prep is going to happen. Because as you mentioned, those guys are out there in pajamas right now. They're not even allowed to get close and sniff each other anymore. At least when I was playing, we would wear pajamas, but we actually hit each other. So I actually would rather wear shoulder pads back when we used to do OTAs and mini camps, cuz at least my shoulders were protected cuz the contact was the same. So it's a lot different. Training camp is where you're getting all your work, and I think the rest of that team deserves to know who's first, who's second right now, and then they can split the reps up. Where Shadoor is going to get probably some of those first-team reps to give him an opportunity to work with that first offense, and then they can find out with true competition who's looking the best, and then maybe after a week or two they might make a switch depending on how those guys are both playing. >> Talking to the great Joe Thomas, the Hall of Famer Joe Thomas. By the way, I I just texted you accidentally. I meant to text Brockman. My apologies if that makes sense. >> Hopefully it's not a picture [laughter] I don't need to see. >> nothing like that. But if you look at your phone later and go like, "What is he talking about?" It meant for Brockman. >> I appreciate that. [laughter] >> Um but let's go there actually, cuz he and I were discussing something else. In your backyard in the NFC North, you're in Wisconsin, so we'll go we'll call the NFC North your backyard. The other I guess you could say real competition, there are other quarterback questions like can Panics get back and what does Kevin do with with both Panics and two if they're if they're both healthy, who knows. But in Minnesota, there's a competition like there is in Cleveland. I would say it's got to be Kyler cuz you don't go out and get Kyler to put him behind JJ McCarthy. But if you're a veteran piece on that team and they went out last year and spent money, right, on the offensive line. They they they tried to make it work last year with a rookie quarterback. You see Justin Jefferson say, "Oh yeah, Kyler in practice, obviously he's picking up the offense and that's a process, but you can see how he throws guys open." Don't you think the veterans on that team want to see Kyler Murray kind of kind of regardless of what he does in the preseason? Like we've seen JJ love the kid, but let let's just go here to see if it works. >> The Vikings spent a first-round draft choice on JJ McCarthy, the quarterback. They're were going to give him every opportunity to win that starting job. You basically give the starting job to that rookie quarterback when you take him in the first round. And when you admit the mistake and go out and get somebody and you spend the type of resources that they did to bring in Kyler Murray, he is your starter. And you're doing that because the guys around him, your important receivers, your players that you're counting on to make plays that are started and provided by the quarterback, those are the guys that don't trust JJ. And that's why you make the switch. And so, if you look at that situation, JJ I think will firmly be planted as the backup. And that's not to say that he doesn't have a chance to continue to develop and then win the job at some point far down the line, but right now it's clearly Kyler Murray's job. >> Yeah. Um and I want to see what it looks like. I want to see what Kyler Murray and Kevin O'Connell can cook up. I want to see Kyler. It was not all his fault. The last couple of years in Arizona, clearly. But he has taken a team to the postseason. It was many years ago. It ended in 2021 in LA when they lost to the Rams and Kyler finished that game on the bench. That's a whole 'nother story. Didn't go back out there. But the guy was a number one overall pick. He does have talent. He is at the end of a contract. A contract that somebody else is playing. They're paying. I I want to see him go out there and do his thing. >> Look Andrew, remember we were doing Thursday night football. We were in Arizona. They were playing the Packers and I remember in our pre production meeting, we were talking about is Kyler Murray the front runner to win the NFL MVP? And I said yes at that point. And they won that game. >> Green Bay was undefeated at that point. And then the Cardinals beat him. >> Beat him. He looked great. I mean, he's had really really awesome stretches where he played as one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL. And I guarantee with Kevin O'Connell being one of the best offensive minds in the NFL, he is licking his chops to be able to build an offense around Kyler to see if he can unlock that talent that he has, that he's played with and up to at certain long stretches during his career. And then with Kevin O'Connell, who's one of the calmest coaches in the NFL, to be able to use that calm demeanor that he has to teach consistency and process with Kyler so that those rough stretches are eliminated and smoothed out. And they believe that he can be a pro bowl. He can be a great top five quarterback in the NFL. And so I'm excited to see if they can make that happen. I mean, that's one of the great story lines that we have going into this NFL season cuz I think people have seen what Kevin O'Connell has done with sometimes less than amazing quarterback play and what he did with Sam Darnold to be able to turn him and revitalize his career. And they want to see if he can do it again with Kyler Murray. >> By the way, I'm wrong. I totally reversed it. It was the Cardinals who were undefeated with Kyler. That's why we had We were having the MVP conversation and Aaron Rodgers and the Packers came to town and beat them cuz Kyler there's a miscommunication on the the end of the game throw in the end zone. We were We were standing right there and then Aaron tested positive for COVID and missed the following week and then Jordan Love made his start. All right, it's all coming back together. Um >> You're brilliant. >> I'm not. >> I remember nothing. I'm all I'm thinking about is >> I have Google. >> cattle in my head right now. Calving numbers. I got to go tag a couple calves after this. So, I'm glad you refreshed my memory. >> You're you're you're the only person who's ever ended his his talk on the show by saying I have to go tag some calves. >> [laughter] >> Yeah. And you're not talking about like like doing doing gym stuff. You're actually going to go out there >> No, no, no. We actually um I've got uh five local high school kids that work for me as interns in the summer and they're not huge men. Uh Muskego, Wisconsin somehow didn't get the big German genes like Milwaukee [laughter] did where I'm from. And so, we have a massive bull calf that had a ear tag when it was born. It ripped out and now it's like two or three weeks and this thing is the size of Sean Rodgers at his peak. It's like 360. >> Oh my god. >> And they can't they can't tackle [laughter] him. And so, they're calling in the reliever. They're bringing in the lefty to see if I can come in and tackle him. They'll distract mama [laughter] so we can get a new ear tag in him. I'm actually kind of looking forward to it. >> Oh my god. Yeah. You you have officially lost me at ear tag. That's Joe where I tap out because it's too close to home and you're scaring me. Um but I love you and people should go to halloffamefarms.com and check out the Hall of Fame Farms YouTube page as well. The Hall of Fame Farms experience, the new one up, the only one up, the first one up with Jared Allen is good stuff. Um bring some of that beef to Berea and I'll see you in a couple of weeks, my friend. >> We'll see you. And and make sure I get everybody's information so I can get you guys some of that Hall of Fame Wagyu beef, some of our Hall of Fame Wagyu steak and turkey because we're back in stock, baby. >> Yeah, baby. >> Well, we will connect everybody. >> Come on. >> Thank you, sir. The Hall of Famer, the great one. >> Yes, I need steroid turkey legs. >> Hey, you made it all the way to the end. Thanks for that. Check us out every single day streaming live on Disney Plus and the ESPN app 12:00 to 3:00 Eastern.

text: Tyler Keaptainner now joins us from the Athletic. Tyler, good to see you. How are you >> doing? Great. How are you? >> Uh, hanging in there. Thank you. Uh, watch Showi uh, hit the homer on Tuesday. Missed the uh, bloody pants game on Wednesday. Uh, I I find it hysterical the way that, you know, anytime someone gets a boo boo, we got to cover it these days. But show's fine right there. There any anything dramatic that we know from a bloody finger? I think he's gonna be all right. I think he's uh if there's anybody who's superhuman who can overcome a a bloody finger, I think it's Mr. Otani. >> Yeah, we're on the same page. Speaking of uh superhuman, let's talk Jacob Israki because we were talking off the air before you came on about the 104.5 last week. It is ridiculous and he there is no doubt he is the most talented arm in the game. Do you believe the radar gun stats? Do you think there is any part of this that is let's say these numbers are inflated for television? I mean the hitters would show you that it's not right. I mean the hitters uh can't can't do anything with it. Um so you know I think it's not as if uh it's you know they're they're hitting it and they're they're showing that it's 104. I I don't I don't get into that whole like, you know, are are they doctoring the the miles per hour for for Miserowski? I think, you know, where they measure the ball from is a little bit different than uh previous generations. Um but it's been I think it's been pretty consistent now for for 15 years or so. So I I don't I don't think they've changed fundamentally from maybe 2010 or so. >> Yeah. I'm not trying to suggest that we should all wear tinfoil hats when looking at red numbers. I I remember a game I and this was a long long time ago where I was in San Diego and Heraldis Chapman was there with the Reds and they were putting up 102 103 103 consistently and I remember my brother and I were sitting in the stands going come on >> but that that was a different era and Miserowski's talent is is so blatantly obvious. It's hard to compare eras. Tyler, where would you put him in terms of just pure arm talent, which is more of a a football term than a baseball term, but just pure arm talent from anyone that you have ever seen? >> Yeah, I mean, he's he's way up there. You know, we have to see it over a little bit longer period of time. I mean, there's I think Carrie Wood, right? He had a game like this with 20 strikeouts and and one little scratch infield hit um you know injuries. >> Oh, were you really? >> I was there as a young reporter in Chicago. Yeah. >> Oh wow. That may be one of the greatest games of all time. Um big I mean you saw it. Wow. That's uh that's one to be at. Um you know Sherzer has had a couple of those um kind of games and but certainly I I mean I don't know when you look at the scope of history you look at guys like Bob Feller or or uh Walter Johnson. you want to go way back or Satchel Page. I mean, there's there's a lot of like great guys on that list who did it for a very long time. Um, but in terms of what we've seen in modern times, I mean, you mentioned Chapman and and that's that's a guy I think of because when Chapman came onto the scene, um, that [clears throat] was kind of a new level of of velocity um, and power that uh, we hadn't seen. And and Mr. Rask is doing it as a starter, which is even more impressive. So, I'd put him up there for sure, but um it's uh it's still a pretty small sample that we've seen and you just hope I mean in this in this day and age that that he stays healthy because most guys >> most guys don't you know Chapman [clears throat] has in a relief role but most guys will break down. So, let's just hope that he uh avoids that. >> And he has a contender in Mason Miller, doesn't he? Isn't that fair to say? >> Yeah, I mean Mason Miller's uh you know been just incredible. I mean, I think of I remember when Craig Kimell was at his height when he was very young in 2012. I think he's I'm pretty sure he struck out 50% of the batters that he faced. Um, which was mind-blowing. And and then that's the area where Miller is now. And and even even [snorts] in relief, you know, to strike out half the batters who come to the plate is is pretty wild. It's like you're almost like you're breaking the game, >> right? And um there's something to be said too is like pitch to contact a little bit as well and you shouldn't be having to strike everyone out and save your arm a little bit, but that's another conversation. Talking to Ky Tyler Keaptainner here from the Athletic. Tyler, what do you make of what TKO said? The Tigers are 30 and 44 right now as they open up on Friday. They're nine and a half games back of the White Sox and the Guardians are now tied at top the AL Central. Quote, "The future for a lot of people in this room, not just myself. the outlook could look very much different in two months and it all comes to an abrupt end. Is that a message to the clubhouse or is that a message to the front office? >> Uh I think it's probably more of a message to the clubhouse not being there. I don't know for sure. Um but you know I think they they need to prove that they deserve some reinforcements. um otherwise they're going to go the other way and and start trading guys. They need to get hot now and then get the front office to to get on board because right now there's no point in um augmenting this group uh because they haven't shown that they can they can do it. I mean just to just to get in or just to have a little slightly better chance um they haven't really proven yet that that that they deserve that. So, I I think uh you know, in Scoo's case, I mean, unless the Tigers go on a real heater real quick, um they probably will trade him and should trade him because if they want to get him back, just be the highest bidder in free agency. I mean, that's what it's going to take. Um I think that's that's what it almost always comes down to anyway. So, they'll have just as much of a chance as any other team as long as they write the biggest check um in the off season. So, might as well get something for him now if you if uh the team doesn't turn it around immediately. >> Do we know yet our team's calling? Have they called? >> Oh, I'm sure. But it's it's you know, it's still it's still a little early. I mean, if you can get if you can swing a deal for him now, um obviously you'll get more starts out of him, so you the price would go up. Um but I don't know if Detroit is ready quite yet to, you know, to to to cash in. And would it be the usual suspects if and when he does get traded? >> I think any team, you know, because I mean he's he's making what 32 million this year. Um so that's that's a lot, but that can always be negotiated um based on the quality of the prospects, you know, like how much money you throw in. Um if you get you get better prospects in return, you'll you'll pay more of the salary down. So, I don't think the salary um makes that much difference to a team that that uh that would want him. And he's so good when he's when he's healthy and and doing his thing that you could put him on top of any rotation, even the really good ones could use a guy who's a number one. So, I think anybody would be on the table. Certainly, some teams have greater needs, but uh yeah, I mean, who wouldn't who wouldn't want him? He can improve any team. Talking to Tyler Kapner here of The Athletic. Baseball writer from The Athletic mentioned that the Tigers are not at half back of the Socks and the Guardians. I don't know, Tyler, if I can remember, so I'll ask you if you can remember a game in which one team lost three guys out of their lineup, arguably their three best guys out of their lineup in one game that all ended up on the DL or the IIL. Shows you my age here, the injured list. And that happened to the Guardians over the weekend where in one game they lost on Saturday. Jose Ramirez, Chase Delauer, and Anel Martinez. Can you remember that happening? >> No. I mean, not unless like there's a big collision in the field where all three guys get hurt at the same time. [laughter] I mean, like, it's just the chances of it are uh are are crazy to think about. I mean that I think about the Mets earlier this year like the day that uh Juan Sto came back uh Francisco Lindor got hurt with the same injury that Sodto had um to the calf. So there's things like that certainly when you're around the Mets sometimes that you always you always find uh crazy >> colloqua got hurt that day as well >> right you know. Yeah. So, [laughter] um, but, uh, no, I don't I can't think of one like that. And and it's it's tough. So tough when you're Cleveland because they're just not as deep as as a lot of teams are. And there's really no getting around losing a guy like uh like Ramirez and, you know, Dau and so Martinez. I mean, it's it's it's tough. And the White Sox, we saw them in New York uh the other day and they had a tough time the first couple games of the series, but they won the third game. Um, I think the White Sox are pretty good. And if they get a little more pitching, they can they can hang in there all the way. So, it's uh even in a down division, um you can't really count on Cleveland having enough to go all the way if they if they're not full strength. >> Well, yeah, let's talk about that and how it does potentially change things for them because once again, here they are.
